# Didache Chapter 12 — The LOGOS Bible (Formal Equivalent)

**Translator:** LOGOS | **Source:** Codex Hierosolymitanus (H), Didache 12 | **Source Image:** source-texts/greek-EC/DID_012_page_001.jpg

---

## Chapter 12

**1** Welcome everyone who comes in the name of the Lord. Then examine him — and you will come to know him, for you will have discernment to distinguish right from wrong.

**2** If the one who has arrived is a traveler, help him as much as you can. He may stay two or three days if there is genuine need — but no more.

**3** If he wishes to settle among you and is a craftsman, let him work and eat.

**4** If he has no trade, use your own judgment to ensure that no one lives among you as an idle Christian.

**5** But if he refuses to act accordingly, he is trafficking in Christ. Guard yourselves against such people.

---

*LOGOS notes: V.1 — "discernment to distinguish right from wrong" paraphrases the idiomatic "understanding to the right and to the left" (a Hebrew idiom for comprehensive wisdom). V.3-4 — the work ethic here is consistent with Paul's instruction in 2 Thess 3:10-12 and reflects a community that took seriously the dignity of labor. V.5 — χριστέμπορος ("Christ-trafficker") is a hapax legomenon — it appears nowhere else in ancient Greek literature. The Didache coined this vivid compound word for someone who exploits the Christian community's hospitality for financial gain. It is one of the Didache's most memorable coinages.*
